response.summary: No, you cannot split a large order into smaller ones to reduce approvals. The policy explicitly prohibits splitting orders to fall under a lower approval limit. Both POL-002 section 2.3 and CON-104 page 3 state that orders must not be split for this purpose.

request.item: split a big order into two smaller ones

reasons.statement: No splitting: An order must not be split into smaller orders to fall under a lower approval limit.
Orders may not be split to stay under this limit.

sources.title: Approval Matrix
sources.text:
An order must not be split into smaller orders to fall under a lower approval limit.
Items requested together for the same purpose count as one order.

sources.title: Lotus Peak supply agreement
sources.text: While on probation, a single purchase order may not exceed INR 5,00,000 including GST. Orders may not be split to stay under this limit. Either party may end this agreement with 30 days' written notice. The Buyer may end it immediately if the Supplier is suspended under the Buyer's vendor policy. Signed for the Buyer by the Head of Procurement, and for the Supplier by its Director of Sales.
